MARKET.head: Seven US regions pursue AVA designations to establish wine identities
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed AVAs across California, Oregon, New Jersey, and New York are in early TTB approval stages; designations take several years and aim to build regional brand recognition and market differentiation.

Annapolis-Sea Ranch in Sonoma (26,637 acres, 651 planted) and Lake Hennessey in Napa (4,495 acres, 355 planted) emphasize Pinot Noir and Cabernet-based blends respectively, defined by fog filtering and air drainage.

Deschutes River in central Oregon (723,760 acres, 77 planted) and Hunterdon Hills in New Jersey (200,000 acres, 12 vineyards) represent first AVA designations for their regions, experimenting with hybrids and aromatic whites suited to their climates.

MARKET.head: Airlines upgrade wine service as premiumization strategy takes flight
MARKET.summ: Nota Bene is a periodic Wine Economist column that briefly highlights stories that might otherwise escape attention. This month we focus on good news stories about wine and wine markets. This isn’t an attempt to paper over the industry’s troubles and challenges.
takeaways: Major US airlines including Delta are expanding wine selections in premium cabins and lounges as part of broader premiumization strategies targeting high-fare passengers.
Wine industry benefits from airline upgrades at a time when quality wines are abundant and competitively priced in the market.
Premium wine access, including Delta One Lounges at major hubs, is being positioned as a lifestyle differentiator to justify higher ticket prices in a K-shaped economy.

MARKET.head: Cruise lines become experiential marketing platform for US wineries
MARKET.summ: From dedicated charters to custom bottlings, wineries are leveraging cruise partnerships to capture engaged audiences and drive long-term sales
takeaways: Cooper's Hawk Winery chartered Virgin Voyages' Valiant Lady for a four-night Caribbean cruise in 2024, integrating its wines across multiple venues and selling out its wine club charter with 30 percent signing up for a February 2027 repeat sailing.
Four Feathers Wine Services developed a custom Columbia Valley brut for Holland America's fleet launched in 2024, which became the cruise line's most-served adult beverage across all ships.

Eleven Eleven Wines hosted 60 guests aboard Scenic Eclipse II in a seven-day Mediterranean sailing and achieved a 33 percent conversion rate among non-wine club passengers, with founders tracking repeat purchases and club memberships as primary success metrics.

MARKET.head: Costco stocks boutique wines as producers struggle to sell
MARKET.summ: Sue and I recently visited our local Costco warehouse store and paused to peruse the wine aisle. We were frankly amazed at the selection we found there. It isn’t just that the prices were very good (that’s not news at Costco, where customers pay an annual membership fee).
takeaways: Costco, the largest US wine retailer, stocks 100-120 wines on a rolling basis including boutique producers and its Kirkland Signature house brand, taking advantage of industry oversupply.

Kirkland Signature wines, launched in 2003, are small lots of around 2000 cases each made by contracted winemakers and distributed across warehouses; inventory turns over frequently to drive repeat visits.
Costco applies the British supermarket model (store-brand wines lending retailer credibility to unfamiliar producers) to the US market, contrasting with typical American reliance on producer brands.

MARKET.head: California and Pacific Northwest vineyards idle acres to survive weak grape market
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: Vineyard idling, a temporary halt to production lasting one to three years, saved northern Willamette Valley producers an average of 38 percent per acre on management costs in a 2025 study of 19 sites.

Mercer Ranches in Prosser, Washington has idled about 1,000 of its 3,350 acres since 2025 as demand for some grape varieties collapsed; Lost Draw Vineyards in Texas High Plains used the pause to replant Pinot Grigio blocks with Picpoul Blanc.

Proper idling requires sustained minimal irrigation, aggressive pruning, weed control, and selective fungicide application to prevent vine damage and enable rapid return to production within two years.

CULTURE.head: Jameson releases single pot still whiskey based on 1826 recipe
CULTURE.summ: Just arrived to the U.S. market, the 46% ABV expression calls back to one of Jameson’s very first recipes
takeaways: Jameson, the world's largest Irish whiskey brand, launched Distiller's Batch, a single pot still expression bottled at 46% ABV, in fall 2025 at $49.99.
The whiskey revives a recipe from an 1826 handwritten mashbill by John Jameson II, using five cask types selected by master distiller Kevin O'Gorman.
Distiller's Batch won gold at the 2025 International Spirits Challenge and double gold at the 2025 San Francisco World Spirits Competition.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A 20 year vertical of Kumeu River’s Hunting Hill Chardonnay
NEWSLETTERS.summ: As tastings go, this was quite a special one, looking at 20 years of New Zealand star winery
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Kumeu River's Hunting Hill Chardonnay vineyard (3.7 hectares, planted 1981-1982) was replanted entirely to clone 15 Chardonnay in 2001 after virus issues; first single-vineyard release was 2006.
Paul Brajkovich confirmed 2020 as perhaps the best vintage ever, scoring 97/100; 2013 frost-affected vintage yielded only 300 cases versus typical 1500.

Winemaking uses whole-bunch pressing, 100% malolactic fermentation, French oak (25% new, except 2010 and 2023 with none new), and aging on lees until January then four months in tank before May bottling.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet Your Robo-Somm
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The year is 2029. First-world civilisation has adapted to mass surveillance. Waymos and Tesla Robotaxis chauffeur NPCs between work and their domicile.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin tested multiple AI wine-pairing apps and found most confuse rosés with reds, ignore vintage variation, and recommend generic brands over appropriate choices.
SommPal, a new food and wine pairing app, ranks up to five wine recommendations per dish with explanatory notes on pairing logic, designed for novice drinkers where sommeliers unavailable.
Developer Marc Lewin stated SommPal is not intended to replace sommeliers but to serve inexperienced wine drinkers in venues lacking expert staff.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Boycott Wines Grown With Herbicides
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Putting Adam Huss’s campaign into practice at the Austrian Single Vineyard Summit
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Adam Huss launched a campaign in August to boycott all wines produced with herbicides, arguing they degrade soil health and decrease wine quality.

Luís Patrão from Vadio winery in Bairrada, Portugal reported that his parents' generation's herbicide use turned vineyards into barren wastelands and eliminated local ladybird, eel, and salamander populations.
The author attended the Austrian Single Vineyard Summit in Grafenegg and used herbicide-free certifications (Organic, Biodynamic, Sustainable Austria) to select wines for tasting.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Heading Out
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Preparing to jump to Italy next week, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker will tour Roero, Piemonte next week tasting wines and handmade foods including cheese, truffle, hazelnut, and honey with seven other American journalists.

Press tour funding mechanics: EU consortiums subsidize regional marketing agencies that contract publicists to identify and invite journalists, making journalists the product acquired for desired press coverage.
Sarah Marsh MW cautioned at the Old Vine Conference that old vines are not universally superior; many carry viruses in scion or rootstock, making blanket preservation advocacy oversimplified.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a separate Wine & Spirits subsection within its Rising and Top lists, breaking it out from the larger Food & Drink category to improve discovery.

Miquel Hudin updated the Wine Substack List (WineStack), now requiring paid subscriptions in active use and human-written text only, removing publications like 'Thirst Behavior' by Bodhi Landa for AI-generated content.
Matthew Jukes, a traditional wine media figure, passed away last month.
